evidence_set: MDMA blood levels were higher with these medicines; with duloxetine and reboxetine the effects were lower at the same time, whereas with bupropion the rated effects were not lower (heart rate was). Duloxetine: peak +14.6%, exposure to 6 hours +16.2%, HMMA peak 40.5% lower. Reboxetine: peak +17.8%, exposure to 24 hours +8.1% (p<.05). Bupropion: peak +14.3%, exposure to 24 hours +33.1% (p<.001), HMMA peak 75.9% lower. For comparison, carvedilol (+4.7%), clonidine (-2.9%), doxazosin (-1.6%) and methylphenidate (-3.5%) changed the peak by 5% or less, and memantine's level at 1 hour was 1.0% lower. Table 6 has no blood-level row for citalopram or fluoxetine.

evidence_set: Methods > Patients and study design, 1st to 3rd paragraphs; Abstract (Methods); Results, 3rd paragraph (last sentence)

Urinary clearance of MDMA was roughly constant across doses (analysis of variance not significant) while non-renal clearance depended on dose (P<0.03) and, in the same eight men, was about halved at 125 mg (38.1 L/h) against 75 mg (74.0 L/h), which the authors read as impaired hepatic clearance; total clearance was 51.1 (SD 14.1) L/h at 125 mg against 86.9 (74.4) L/h at 75 mg. The SDs of non-renal clearance are cut off at the edge of the table image.

Across the five doses (50 to 150 mg, a 3-fold range), with different men at 50, 100 and 150 mg and the same eight men at 75 and 125 mg, the AUC(0-24 h) of MDMA ranged from 100.1 to 5232.0 ug.h/L (more than 10-fold): two men at 50 mg had 100.1 and 813.9 ug.h/L, two men at 150 mg 5132.8 and 5232.0, with peak concentrations 441.9 and 486.9 ug/L at 150 mg against a mean of 236.4 at 125 mg. A Kruskal-Wallis test of dose-normalized AUC(0-infinity) across the five doses was only marginal (P<0.1).

evidence_set: In all studies that assessed cannabis in conjunction with alcohol, the estimated odds ratio for the combination was higher than for cannabis alone; the authors take this to suggest synergy, cite four sources and give no estimates. The comparison is with cannabis alone, so it does not separate an additive from a more-than-additive combination, since alcohol raises the odds on its own. The review's pooled estimates are for cannabis-only drivers (THC with no alcohol or other drug present; one study relied on self-report alone).

evidence_set: Randomized, double-blind, four-arm crossover (placebo, ethanol, GHB, both; single fixed doses, study conditions) in healthy adults who drank lightly and had little GHB experience: 22 enrolled, 16 completed. Oxygen saturation fell with all three active conditions relative to placebo; the combination gave the largest drop, maximal mean change −2.12 ± 0.34 percentage points from baseline at 90 minutes, greater than placebo (P < 0.0001), GHB alone (P = 0.027) and ethanol alone (P = 0.013); saturation stayed below baseline for the 4 hours of monitoring with all three. Fig 2, read by eye (approximate): combination about −2.2 and GHB alone about −1.6 at 90 minutes. No interaction test or baseline saturation is given; the ± after −2.12 is not labelled in the text, and the Fig 2 caption says its error bars are 95% confidence intervals.
